overview: Docket (1933-34) on Japanese wireless interference with US Army and Navy radio: a proposed Tokyo conference Japan resisted, debate over routing complaints diplomatically, and mixed results for naval versus Army stations.

people.name: Fred P. Andrews
people.role: Captain; proposed War Department representative at the contemplated Tokyo radio conference

people.name: Henry Latrobe Roosevelt
people.role: Assistant Secretary of the U.S. Navy; associated with the Navy Department entry of September 15

subfiles.title: First list of papers on wireless telegraph interference in Japan
subfiles.about: An index summarizes correspondence concerning Japanese interference with American military radio stations and proposals for an informal technical conference in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Docket (1933-34) covers a proposed Tokyo radio conference Japan resisted, and worsening Army-station interference despite naval gains.

subfiles.title: Duplicate list of papers on wireless telegraph interference in Japan
subfiles.about: A second copy of the file index repeats the chronology of official correspondence about Japanese radio interference and the proposed Tokyo conference.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate docket repeats the Tokyo radio-conference dispute, with a minor despatch-number discrepancy.

interest: Shows 1933-34 US-Japan friction over Japanese radio interference with American military communications in Asia.
